source.title: Booster: Tackling Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Attenuating Harmful Perturbation
source.authors: Tian-Sheng Huang; Si-Hao Hu; Fatih Ilhan; S. Tekin; Ling Liu

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates harmful fine-tuning using harmful-output scores, but does not reproduce the original studies’ exact experiments and also evaluates an alignment-stage defense.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmful-output scores after fine-tuning with harmful data, including mixed harmful and benign datasets, and reports effects of pure harmful versus pure SST2 fine-tuning. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localizing weights, or safety depth. Results cited from other work are not included. The number-of-harmful-samples sweep in Table 8 concerns samples used during alignment, not harmful user fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: The vanilla SFT baseline fine-tunes the authors' own SFT-aligned Llama2-7B, Gemma2-9B and Qwen2-7B on benign task data mixed with 50–250 BeaverTails harmful examples, and reports the rate of unsafe outputs judged by a moderation model. That bears directly on V1. A pure-SST2 run, shown only in a figure, bears on V2. The method differs from the originals: LoRA, fine-tuning lr 1e-5, harmful data diluted in 80–95% benign data, and an in-house SFT safety alignment rather than vendor chat models. Nothing bears on V3–V7. Booster is a defense, not a depth-spreading method.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors argue harmful perturbation, a gradient step on harmful data, lowers harmful loss and breaks alignment. Booster, an alignment-stage regularizer, attenuates this and lowers post-fine-tuning HS while keeping fine-tune accuracy. They also concede HS still rises with the harmful ratio under Booster, and that Booster is sensitive to the hyperparameters λ and α.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes aligned models on mixed harmful and benign data and measures unsafe-output scores, but its focus is an alignment-stage defense and its experimental setup differs from the original studies. It does not test token-position KL or opening-token bypasses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported harmful score changes with harmful-data ratio, total fine-tuning sample count, fine-tuning dataset, model, and Booster hyperparameters λ and α. The paper notes that optimal hyperparameters differ across downstream tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful gradient steps sharply reduce harmful training and test loss. Pure SST2 steps slightly increase harmful loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Harmful-gradient perturbation, by lowering loss on harmful responses, drives post-fine-tuning safety loss; benign classification gradients do not.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR); the text refers to ICLR2025 submissions and reviewers.
record.problems: The paper reports no uncertainty intervals or significance tests for the harmful-score results. Harmful Score uses one moderation model. The text does not state results across multiple random seeds. Several loss and score curves are figure-only and have no extractable numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 results for Lisa and RepNoise are omitted. Table 3 and Table 4 results for Lisa, RepNoise, and Vaccine are omitted. These are defense-comparator results; the retained rows prioritize SFT, Booster, sample-count variation, and model/task variation. Table 1 clean-condition values are retained for SFT, Lisa, RepNoise, Vaccine, and Booster.

untested.parts: Vendor safety-tuned chat models (e.g., Llama-2-chat, GPT-3.5); full-parameter fine-tuning; pure harmful sets of 10–100 examples with readable numbers; models other than three 7–9B open models aligned in-house by SFT.
Benign instruction or chat data such as Alpaca or Dolly; carefully selected benign data; any benign task beyond SST2 classification without harmful data mixed in.
Localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Causes of shallowness. The harmful-gradient argument concerns fine-tuning degradation, not token depth.
Training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: SFT clean (p=0) HS 1.30 after benign SST2 fine-tuning. It is used as a baseline but has no row of its own; it bears on V2.
Undefended SFT HS on GSM8K across harmful ratio p=0.05–0.2 (14.8, 23.2, 32.4, 40.0) and sample count n=500–2000 (10.6, 23.2, 41.6, 58.6). Not declared in rows_left_out.
Undefended SFT HS on GSM8K for Gemma2-9B (26.4) and Qwen2-7B (37.9).
HS of the aligned Gemma2-9B before fine-tuning (SFT 1.5). This is the pre-attack baseline for T4-SFT-Gemma.
SFT HS curve over fine-tuning steps at 10% harmful data, still rising after 2000 steps (figure only).

record.verdict_notes: Defense-comparator and Booster rows are re-linked to none: they measure defended models, the study's own method or competing defenses, not the claim. The 'aligned' models are the authors' own SFT safety alignment of the open base models on BeaverTails, which may be weaker than vendor RLHF. The GSM8K SFT HS for the default setting disagrees within the paper: 14.80 in Table 3 versus 23.20 in Tables 10–12. HS comes from a single moderation-model judge, with no seeds or uncertainty reported. Threshold used for states: observed where a majority of outputs are harmful (HS ≥60).

versions.untested_parts: The study tests mixtures containing 50–500 harmful fine-tuning examples, but not every dataset or training setup covered by the claim.
It reports pure SST2 fine-tuning; it does not test carefully selected benign instruction data or a range of benign instruction datasets.
Per-token KL divergence and response-position concentration.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
Why safety behavior is shallow; the paper instead studies harmful-gradient perturbations as a cause of safety degradation after fine-tuning.
Training to spread safety beyond the first tokens and whether that effect holds up.
